Most people trying to sell AI are fighting over the same few thousand customers who'd rather build their own tools. Meanwhile there are multi-million dollar businesses on Main Street that just want more jobs, more calls, and less headaches. That's the opening.
In this video I break down the full system for selling AI services to boring local businesses: find a market, score each business by what's broken, pick the best ones, and pitch them with a custom asset.
Why boring businesses are the best clients almost nobody wants: they're high ticket (one HVAC job is 12k to 20k), they don't churn, they're not saturated, and you're talking straight to the owner. You're not creating demand with ads or SEO. You're helping them convert the traffic they already have.

entry.title: The best AI business doesn't touch AI

media:group.media:title: The best AI business doesn't touch AI
media:group.media:description:
The biggest AI opportunity right now isn't another app. it's using AI marketing skills in a boring local trade where nobody else can run an ad.
How to actually start: 1. open google maps, search "pool service" or "hvac" in your city. 30+ companies with 100+ reviews = demand that already exists. 2. pick a trade you have zero interest in. boring is the point, it means less competition. 3. find the operator who's great at the work and bad at marketing. you bring customers, they do the job. 4. don't learn the trade or buy a truck. own the front end only: seo, ads, automation. 5. run one simple ad with a real job photo, not a designed one. optimize for the phone call, not clicks.
You're not creating demand. You're carving off a slice that's already there.

entry.title: The "false productivity" trap killing your AI projects

media:group.media:title: The "false productivity" trap killing your AI projects
media:group.media:description:
AI turned building into the easy part, the real trap now is false productivity: endless dopamine, and a project that never ships.
You get a win every few prompts, so you keep going. Two weeks later you're still deep in it and can't even say what problem you started with.
The way out is setting your gates before you start:
1. Write a phased PRD where "done" is an actual gate. You don't start the next thing until you've hit it.
2. Ship the MVP and let the market tell you if it's real, instead of building out every case first.
3. Pick a launch date and ship whatever you've got when it comes.
Building will always feel like progress. Shipping is the only thing that proves it.
